entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This claim petition is filed U/s 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a RTA.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 17.12.2023 at about 2.15 p.m, when the petitioner was riding his Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-13-EH-3649 along with one Shivakumar as a pillion rider, on the left side of NH-75 road, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

When they reached near Kannaghatta village divider, NH-75 road, Bellur Hobli,
Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, at that time all of a sudden the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA- 41-ME-5575 came from Bengaluru side in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.

Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, wherein he took first aid and thereafter he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and he was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
It is specifically urged that due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
It is further urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel, he failed to contest the matter by filing the written statement.
4. After service of notice, respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent admitted the issuance of Bundled Auto Secure Private car insurance policy in respect of car.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Further the respondent has contended that, the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 147, 149, 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the rider of motorcycle who was riding the said vehicle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle and petitioner did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.

On account of willful breach of the terms &
conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :

entities.text: ISSUES Ranju M P vs R P Conmix
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 17.12.2023 at about 2.15 p.m, near Kannaghatta village divider,
NH-75 road, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-ME-5575 ?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 13 were marked on his behalf.
The MRO was examined as PW.2, through him got marked Ex.P.14 & 15 documents.

In order to prove the defence,
the respondent No.2 examined its official as RW.1, through him got marked Ex.R.1 document.
7.
Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.2 on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1:
The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.15 lakhs together.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of the car for the offences punishable under section's 279, 337 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.2 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Therefore, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the car.

In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 3 SCC 646.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered in the 'Affirmative'.
9. ISSUE NO.2 : As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : 1)
CLW 5x1 cm over the scalp occipital region 2) Abrasion of whole of the lateral aspect of left forearm 3) Abrasion over the left leg.
The doctor opined that the said injuries are simple in nature.
Ex.P.9 being the Discharge Summary wherein it discloses that the petitioner was taken treatment as an inpatient from 20.12.2023 to 22.12.2023 for a period of 3 days.
During the course of treatment he treated conservatively.

Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :

sentences.text: 10. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY & LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD :
The petitioner has deposed that he was working as Agriculturist and milk vendor and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m, and due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
However he has neither proved his avocation nor his earning capacity.
However he has neither examined the doctor nor produced disability certificate to substantiate the fact he has become permanently disabled.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be accepted that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
Though PW.1 deposed in his evidence affidavit that due to the injuries sustained in the accident he was unable to continue avocation and thereby he sustained loss of income from this accident.
So also no iota of evidence is placed on record to show that he has sustained loss of income during treatment period.
Non-production of the any documents in this regard results in drawing of an inference that he has not suffered any financial loss during the period of his treatment.

Therefore no compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the heads of 'Loss of future income due to disability' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
11.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
The period of hospitalization of 3 days is proved.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day and a sum of Rs.3,600/- (1,200 X 3) is awarded under this head.
12. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.15,000/- under this head.
13. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

As per the bills marked at Ex.P11, the petitioner has spent Rs.20,925/-
towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of his cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.21,000/- towards medical expenses.
14. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
There is no disability, therefore no amount was awarded to the petitioner under this head.
15. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.

16. The calculation table stands as follows:

Attendant charges, extra nutritious : 3,600-00 food & conveyance charges 4 Pain & sufferings : 15,000-00 5
Medical expenses : 21,000-00 6 Loss of future amenities & : - Nil - happiness 7
Future medical expenses : - Nil -  Total 39,600-00
17. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
18. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the RC owner and insurer of the car thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
19. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.39,600/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.
After deposit of compensation amount the office is directed to release the entire share with interest of the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E- payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
